The one defect shape behind all three of today's merges

Machinery that reports success while doing nothing

#3386: hooks logged to a gate that dropped the line. #3389: a guard enforced a taxonomy it could not verify applied. #3393: docs advertised a feature that could not exist. In all three the gate that should have caught it also could not fail — the settings test had six cases and only "valid JSON" was capable of failing.

That is the thesis of the milestone, and it is why "tests pass" was worth less than it looked. Both new tests assert effects rather than calls: the dispatcher test asserts bytes on disk at the default log level, and the settings test was control-verified to fail when a retired key returns.

All 20 open issues, grouped by the lane that decides whether they can run in parallel. The lane is set by generated-output footprint, not by topic — two items that both regenerate src/hooks/dist/ will conflict the moment either merges, which is exactly what happened between #3386 and #3389 today.

Why this order

11 first — target verified and observed firing this session (I used AskUserQuestion repeatedly), it deletes a whole MCP server, and it frees a permanent tool slot. Highest certainty, real payoff, no shared generated output.

09 and 13 next — both targets confirmed in the binary, both are self-contained hook deletions, and 13 additionally removes an rm -rf that runs without holding git worktree lock on an estate that currently has 19 live worktrees.

08 last — it is the only one whose retirement would rewrite the protocol this session is itself running inside. Do it when no other v10 lane is mid-flight.

What #3311 gains from this

ork's ork.settings.json sandbox block was authored against failIfUnavailable, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed and friends, and those keys all ship in the binary. So the block is inert because it sits in a scope CC does not read for those keys — not because it targets invented settings. The fix (set them where CC reads them) is viable rather than a phantom, which moves #3311 from "investigate" to "implement".

The methodological trap, stated plainly

Keybindings would have returned HIT on every string involved — keybindings, the file path, the schema. It was still impossible, because what was missing was not a string but an action in a closed enumeration. Existence probes are cheap and I ran them; the fitness probe is the one that decides, and it has to be written per mechanism. For the four ⚠️ rows in the removal order, that means: does the / menu resolve /ork:doctor with the wrappers disabled (06); does a 10-agent run complete with no hook denial after moving 44 guards to hooks.json (07).

Right now herdr holds 8 live agents, and exactly one is in orchestkit (this session, w6:p1). The other seven are in core, platform and hq-ext-plugin. So capacity is not the constraint — merge-lane contention is.

The rule that actually governs parallelism

Partition by generated-output footprint, not by topic

Measured today: #3386 and #3389 were topically unrelated and both regenerated src/hooks/dist/ + plugins/. The instant the first merged, the second went CONFLICTING/DIRTY on generated files alone, and the fix was to reset onto the new main, replay 7 source files and rebuild. Hand-resolving bundles is theatre — the build is the authoritative resolution.

So: one in-flight PR per lane, at most. Lane C and Lane I have no generated output and can run as wide as you like.

lane   generated output                       parallelism      seed issue
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
H      src/hooks/dist/ + plugins/             1 in flight      #3391 then #3311
S      plugins/skills/ + docs-search-index    1 in flight      #3313
C      none (.github/workflows only)          unbounded        #3332 + #3333
I      none (read-only, writes a report)      unbounded        #3352 #3353 #3335 #3336

Concrete herdr wiring

One workspace per lane, each agent in its own git worktree so node_modules and HEAD never thrash. Note each worktree needs its own npm install — the kb worktree failed its first build today for exactly that.

# one worktree per lane (inside the repo — a sibling path gets silently cd-reset)
WT=$(~/.claude/hooks/worktree-new.sh laneC fix/3332-release-topology origin/main) && cd "$WT"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund

# park an agent in it and hand it the task
herdr workspace create --name laneC
herdr agent start   --workspace laneC --agent claude
herdr agent prompt  --workspace laneC "Fix #3332 ... open a PR with Closes #3332"
herdr agent wait    --workspace laneC --state idle,done

# read the result without attaching
herdr agent read    --workspace laneC | tail -40

Two things I would not delegate

The merge button. Lane H and Lane S serialize on generated output, so merges must be ordered by one coordinator that rebuilds after each landing. An agent that merges its own PR the moment CI is green will strand its siblings — and with 8 live agents an auto-merge cascade can land another session's work.

Mechanism 08 (worktree protocol). Retiring it rewrites the protocol every other agent is running inside. Single-threaded, no siblings in flight.

Honest gaps. The lane assignments are derived from which files each issue names, not from a measured build-output diff per issue — I verified the footprint rule on exactly one pair (#3386 / #3389) and generalised it. The wave table is a plan, not a schedule; no effort estimate here is measured, and #3336 exists precisely because the audit asserted costs it never measured. Do not let this page become the next thing that claims more than it did.
